name: Gold Playbook
tagline: Gold's prop-firm reality in 2026: a dollar range that tripled in two years, news bursts that make firms suspend whole product complexes, the London-breakout and sweep-fade playbook with its measured exceptions — and the 1–2 MGC sizing that keeps a $2,000 floor alive.
summary: Gold is the fastest-growing prop instrument and the one the rulebooks punish hardest. The measurements: average daily range went from ~$33 (2024) to ~$120+ (2026) in dollars, one-in-ten sessions now move more than $150, and a single ordinary GC futures session's median range exceeds a sixth of a $2,000 drawdown — which is why the prop sizing unit is MGC at 1–2 contracts, or 0.05–0.20 CFD lots. The tradeable structure is real and specific: Asian compression resolved by London, sweeps that fade into the opposite pool, break-retest after a *close* (gold fakes out by reputation), and news windows quantified down to the median first-5-minute move. The counterweights are all documented: a working paper's bare-rule test of supply/demand zones hit targets below breakeven, prop firms froze all metals for months during the 2026 volatility spike without notice dates, ±2-minute execution windows confiscate profits on fills you didn't choose, and the forum's own gold blowup stories share one plot — the revenge trade after the sweep. This guide is gold's prop game: setups, volatility math, sizing, and availability risk, each with its source class attached.
oneLiner: Trade the Asia-range resolution with close-confirmed entries, size 1–2 MGC against the floor, calendar every Tier-1 print, and accept that gold's availability is itself a regime.
keyQuote: Gold resolves one side, reverses, then resolves the other — straddling the range is reliably two losses.
lead: Gold trades like a macro event with an intraday personality — the guide to surviving both halves is measured numbers, fixed windows, and micros.
highlights: The dollar range tripled in two years — a 2024-sized stop now sits inside an ordinary 2026 day; re-scale from current data, monthly.
Asia compresses ($10–25), London resolves (15-min close beyond + volume confirmation), NY continues — and the pre-data window and rollover hour are where the fakes live.
News days are ordinary days with a burst: 3–5× an hour's range in the first 5 minutes, whole-day range only ~1.2×; the release window, not the day, is the risk.
Mechanical supply/demand zones measured below breakeven without filters — trend alignment and room-to-target are the trade, the rectangle is not.
One GC session's median range is ~$3,164 — 1.5× a full 50K eval drawdown. MGC at $10/oz, 1–2 contracts, is the same chart at survivable risk.
Firms suspended the entire metals complex mid-2026 for months, and ±2-minute execution windows count *fills you didn't initiate* as violations.

articles.title: Average daily range of XAUUSD 2026 (full method)
articles.takeaway: $31 (2020) → $33 (2024) → $61 (2025) → $120.5 (2026) dollar ranges; ATR-scaled bands held ~89% containment across regimes while fixed-dollar stops failed silently.

articles.title: Gold daily range tool & tables
articles.takeaway: Independent tick-data cross-check: 2026 avg $122 / median $100, widest $771, 1-in-10 days >$152.

articles.title: Gold news days: NFP, CPI, FOMC measured
articles.takeaway: First-5-min medians $17–22 at releases vs $4–6 ordinary; days are ordinary-with-a-burst (whole-day range only ×1.14–1.27); price runs ≥$20 from pre-release on 90–95% of release days.

articles.title: Gold after the news (fill/held rates)
articles.takeaway: Median 5-min moves NFP $9.03 / CPI $9.13 / FOMC $6.04; first move held at 60 min on 68–83% of releases.

articles.title: Gold on CPI days (study)
articles.takeaway: Release hour ×1.94 range; first move reversed by close ~29%; day-after goes against CPI direction 61% — CPI-day biases don't carry.

articles.title: XAUUSD supply & demand zones (scripted test)
articles.takeaway: Bare mechanical zones hit 2R on only 26% of first touches — below the ~33% breakeven; includes a published correction for roll-gap contamination.

articles.title: XAUUSD session breakout (mechanics)
articles.takeaway: Asia $10–25 compression, London resolution rules (15-min close + 1.5× volume), the >50%-of-ATR overnight skip, and the never-straddle warning.

articles.title: Gold break & retest guide
articles.takeaway: Gold's false-breakout reputation codified: require a close beyond ≥0.25×ATR; wick-through-close-back is a grab, strong body is intent.

articles.title: Liquidity sweep trading on gold (Judas Swing)
articles.takeaway: London almost always sweeps one side before the real move; fade only after structure close; double sweeps common — and counter-trend sweeps in a higher-timeframe trend are continuations.

articles.title: Prop firms that allow gold futures (rules tracked)
articles.takeaway: All seven checked futures firms list GC/MGC with caps (Apex 6 minis, Topstep GC-3 volatile-metals cap, MFFU 5 metal micros); measured MGC session median $31.6; Feb–May 2026 metals suspension forensics; firm close times and hedging groups.

articles.title: MGC contract specifications & margin tracker
articles.takeaway: MGC 10oz, $0.10 = $1.00/tick, $10 per $1 move; CME moved metals margin to %-of-notional and raised it through the 2026 spike; sim props replace margin with drawdown + caps.

articles.title: FTMO trading conditions update — XAUUSD news window
articles.takeaway: The explicit ±2-minute execution window, profit confiscation on in-window fills, and gold's seconds-fast moves as the stated reason.

articles.title: CME daily metals volume bulletin
articles.takeaway: One trading day: MGC 336K vs GC 196K vs QO 2.2K vs SGU 3 contracts — the liquidity map that picks your contract.

articles.title: Notice: metals trading halt & return (community records)
articles.takeaway: The availability-risk episode in traders' own words: halt Feb 2026, back ~May, caps changed, no official date tables — instrument access as regime risk.

articles.title: Faked out by gold twice (r/propfirm)
articles.takeaway: The canonical failure sequence, documented: sweep → revenge-size → daily-limit breach across four accounts, weeks of $200–300/day progress erased in one afternoon.
